questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with episodes of melena containing gastric mucosa and acute, intermittent pain in the right iliac fossa. On surgical exploration, a characteristic structure is identified. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of melena (bloody stool) containing ectopic gastric mucosa in a young child is pathognomonic for Meckel's diverticulum. Meckel's is a true diverticulum resulting from the incomplete obliteration of the vitelline duct. The presence of gastric mucosa produces acid, leading to ulceration and painless bleeding. Intermittent pain can occur if the diverticulum causes intussusception. An appendicular lump (Option B) presents with fever and constant pain, not gastric-induced melena. Carcinoid tumors (Option C) are rare in children and present with systemic symptoms like flushing. Obstructed bowel (Option D) would show persistent vomiting and distension rather than isolated melena. Following the "Rule of 2s," Meckel's occurs in 2% of the population, is 2 inches long, and is located 2 feet from the ileocecal valve. Thus, the specific findings confirm Meckel's diverticulum
questions.learning: The clinical presentation of melena (bloody stool) containing ectopic gastric mucosa in a young child is pathognomonic for Meckel's diverticulum. Meckel's is a true diverticulum resulting from the incomplete obliteration of the vitelline duct.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following is a remnant of embryological hindgut in the pre-rectal area?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Tailgut cyst

A tailgut cyst (retrorectal cystic hamartoma) is a congenital lesion arising from persistent remnants of the embryonic hindgut (postanal gut). It is typically located in the presacral (retrorectal/pre-rectal) space and may present with pelvic pain, recurrent infection, constipation, or a palpable mass. Although usually benign, malignant transformation can occur, making complete surgical excision the treatment of choice.

Why not the other options?

• A. Chordoma: Arises from remnants of the embryonic notochord, usually in the sacrococcygeal region or clivus.
• C. Epidermoid cyst: Results from ectodermal inclusion and contains squamous epithelium without skin appendages.
• D. Dermoid cyst: A germ cell lesion containing ectodermal derivatives such as hair follicles and sebaceous glands; not derived from the hindgut.
questions.learning: Tailgut cyst — A tailgut cyst (retrorectal cystic hamartoma) is a congenital lesion arising from persistent remnants of the embryonic hindgut (postanal gut).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 45-year-old man presented to Ayushman Arogya Mandir with blood pressure measurements of 148/93 and 153/99 on two separate occasions. What is the next step in management?
options: Admit the patient and give IV antihypertensives
Start the patient on Amlodipine 5mg per day and follow up after 1 month
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Start the patient on Amlodipine 5mg per day and follow up after 1 month

Blood pressure readings ≥140/90 mmHg on two separate occasions confirm hypertension.

As per NPCDCS / Ayushman Arogya Mandir guidelines, uncomplicated Stage 1–2 hypertension is managed at the primary level by initiating first-line antihypertensive therapy (e.g., Amlodipine 5 mg daily) with follow-up after 1 month for titration and monitoring.
questions.learning: Start the patient on Amlodipine 5mg per day and follow up after 1 month Blood pressure readings ≥140/90 mmHg on two separate occasions confirm hypertension.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient came with complaints of palpitations and dyspnea for 4 hours. On ECG, he was found to have atrial fibrillation with no other cardiovascular symptoms. What is the next best step in management?
options: Look for left atrial thrombus with carotid doppler
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ventricular rate control

ECG shows Atrial Fibrillation (AF).

AF is characterized by:

• Irregularly irregular rhythm
• Absent P waves
• Fibrillatory baseline

This is acute atrial fibrillation (<48 hours) without hemodynamic instability or severe symptoms.

Initial management is ventricular rate control using AV nodal blockers.

Drugs Used for Rate Control

| Drug | Mechanism

| ---- | ---------

| Beta blockers | Slow AV node conduction

| Non-DHP calcium blockers | AV node blockade

| Digoxin | ↑ vagal tone → slows AV node

Emergent cardioversion is reserved for instability, and anticoagulation/thrombus evaluation is considered later.

Thus, rate control is the next best step.

| Situation | Management

| --------- | ----------

| Unstable AF | DC cardioversion

| Stable AF | Rate control

| Long-term | Anticoagulation
questions.learning: Ventricular rate control ECG shows Atrial Fibrillation (AF). AF is characterized by: • Irregularly irregular rhythm • Absent P waves • Fibrillatory baseline This is acute atrial fibrillation (<48 hours) without hemodynamic instability or severe symptoms.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: Which anatomical plane, located between the rectus abdominis muscle and the transversalis fascia, contains the neurovascular structures that supply the abdominal wall?
options: Between the internal oblique and external oblique
Between the internal oblique and rectus abdominis
Between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis
questions.explanation: The abdominal wall is composed of several muscle layers, and the primary neurovascular structures (including the lower intercostal, subcostal, and iliohypogastric nerves) travel within a specific anatomical plane. This neurovascular plane is situated between the internal oblique and the transversus abdominis muscles. This is analogous to the intercostal space where the neurovascular bundle travels between the internal and innermost intercostal muscles. Option A (between internal and external oblique) and Option C (between internal oblique and rectus) do not house the primary nerve trunks. Option B (deep to transversus abdominis) refers to the preperitoneal space. Understanding this plane is clinically vital for surgeons when performing abdominal incisions or for anesthesiologists performing a TAP (Transversus Abdominis Plane) block, where local anesthetic is injected exactly into this space to provide regional analgesia. Therefore, the plane between the two deepest flat muscles of the abdomen is the correct anatomical answer
questions.learning: The abdominal wall is composed of several muscle layers, and the primary neurovascular structures (including the lower intercostal, subcostal, and iliohypogastric nerves) travel within a specific anatomical plane.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following muscles are supplied by the lateral plantar nerve? Options: 1. Abductor hallucis 2. Flexor digitorum accessorius 3. Flexor hallucis brevis 4. First lumbrical 5. First interossei
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2 and 5

The correct answer is 2 and 5.

The lateral plantar nerve supplies most intrinsic sole muscles, including flexor digitorum accessorius (quadratus plantae) and the interossei (via its deep branch).

Abductor hallucis and the first lumbrical are supplied by the medial plantar nerve, while flexor hallucis brevis has dual supply but its medial head is medial plantar—hence excluded here.
questions.learning: 2 and 5 The correct answer is 2 and 5. The lateral plantar nerve supplies most intrinsic sole muscles, including flexor digitorum accessorius (quadratus plantae) and the interossei (via its deep branch).
